items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: But when we spoke to and talked with a Negro soldier who was from the North and stationed at an army camp near Orlando, he was not happy to be in the South.

ctx.x: When we played in Orlando, Fla, we met a very nice white fellow who owned a five and ten cent store. He was saying: 'Yes, sir' and 'No, sir' to us. The reason is that he was from the North and he has a certain respect for us and he was happy to see us in his store.

But when we spoke to and talked with a Negro soldier who was from the North and stationed at an army camp near Orlando, he was not happy to be in the South. There was a curfew for Negro soldier and they had to be back at their camp or off the streets by 9 pm.

We played a dance in Tampa, Fla, and this night Sissle must have known that George Wingfield and I were drinking on the stand but he could not afford to make himself ridiculous by trying to find out if it was true. George was and had been for a long time a very heavy drinker and he had drank so much in days gone by, that he looked as though he was always pickled.
